banner.headline: Discover the design language that feels like you.
banner.quote: “Architecture is more than choosing a style. It is about how you want to feel, live, interact and experience a space.”
banner.badge: 5 questions · 60 seconds · Discover your Design Matrix

questions.title: What kind of space draws you in?
questions.subtitle: Imagine these spaces. Which ones would you most enjoy coming home to? (Choose up to 2 options)

options.label: Calm & Refined
options.desc: Clean lines, uncluttered surfaces, neutral colours and soft natural light.

options.label: Warm & Inviting
options.desc: Wood, textured surfaces, warm lighting and comfortable, welcoming spaces.

options.label: Bold & Dramatic
options.desc: Strong geometry, statement materials, dramatic lighting and a sense of grandeur.

options.label: Connected to Nature & Deeply Relaxing
options.desc: Natural materials, greenery, filtered light and a strong connection between indoors and outdoors.

questions.endNote: Architectural insight: The feeling of a space comes from more than furniture or decoration. Proportion, light, material, colour, texture and spatial openness all contribute to its atmosphere.

questions.title: Which material combination feels most like you?
questions.subtitle: If you had to choose the material language of your home, which combination would you naturally gravitate towards? (Choose 1 option)

options.label: Stone + Wood + Linen
options.desc: Natural stone, timber, soft fabrics and restrained colours.

options.label: Concrete + Glass + Metal
options.desc: Exposed concrete, glass, metal and clean architectural surfaces.

options.label: Marble + Wood + Brass
options.desc: Rich stone, timber, brass details and carefully controlled lighting.

options.label: Plaster + Terracotta + Timber
options.desc: Earthy plaster finishes, terracotta, timber and handcrafted textures.

options.label: Timber, clay, terrazzo, cane, plants & natural stone
options.desc: A rich combination of natural materials, greenery and varied textures.
options.img: /matrix/Q2_E Timber, clay, terrazzo, cane, plants & natural stone.jpg

options.label: Coloured tile, patterned fabric, painted surfaces & furniture
options.desc: Colour, pattern and furniture become important parts of the design.
options.img: /matrix/Q2_F Coloured tile, patterned fabric, painted surfaces.jpg

options.label: Subtle & muted colours, soft fabric, rattan & minimal furniture
options.desc: Calm neutral tones, lightweight natural textures and simple furniture.
options.img: /matrix/Q2_G Subtle muted colours, soft fabric, rattan, minimal furniture.jpg

questions.endNote: Architectural insight: Materiality is not simply about colour. Texture, reflectivity, scale, warmth, ageing and the way materials meet each other influence how a space is experienced.

questions.title: How do you prefer to live?
questions.subtitle: Think about your everyday life rather than how you want your home to look. You can choose up to 2 options.

options.label: I prefer order and want everything to have a place.
options.desc: You may benefit from integrated storage, clean circulation and a reduced material palette.

options.label: I spend time outdoors and want nature to be part of daily life.
options.desc: You may benefit from courtyards, shaded terraces, large openings and garden connections.

options.label: I enjoy hosting, displaying objects and changing my surroundings.
options.desc: You may benefit from flexible rooms, strong focal points and adaptable lighting.
options.img: /matrix/Q3_C Hosting (Flexible room with a strong focal point dining).jpg

options.label: I value openness, flexibility and a slightly unconventional atmosphere.
options.desc: You may benefit from open planning, robust materials and expressive structural elements.

options.label: I want a home that feels settled, familiar and built to last.
options.desc: You may benefit from balanced proportions, durable finishes and references to local architecture.

options.label: I like grandeur and want every space to feel like a feature.
options.desc: You may benefit from distinct spaces, strong architectural details and layered lighting.

questions.endNote: Architectural insight: Good architecture begins with understanding how a person actually lives. Storage, circulation, indoor–outdoor connections, flexibility, focal points and proportions can be designed around lifestyle.

questions.title: How much personality should your home show?
questions.subtitle: Imagine someone visiting your home for the first time. Which statement feels closest to you? Choose 1 option.

options.label: "I want my home to feel calm and uncluttered."
options.desc: I prefer simplicity, consistency and visual quiet.

options.label: "I want my home to feel carefully curated."
options.desc: I like a clean base with selected artwork, objects and details.
options.img: /matrix/Q4_B Carefully curated (Clean base with a few selected artworks).jpg

options.label: "I want my home to tell my story."
options.desc: I enjoy collecting things, displaying memories and bringing individuality into my surroundings.
options.img: /matrix/Q4_C Tells my story (Eclectic, displaying memories collections).jpg

options.label: "I want my home to make a statement."
options.desc: I enjoy distinctive forms, colours, materials or architectural features that create a strong impression.
options.img: /matrix/Q4_D Make a statement (Distinctive, striking architectural feature).jpg

questions.endNote: Architectural insight: Personal expression does not necessarily mean more decoration. It can come through art, colour, material, architecture, lighting or the way spaces are composed.

questions.title: What do you want your home to feel like 10 years from now?
questions.subtitle: Choose the option that resonates most with your long-term vision.

options.label: Timeless
options.desc: I want it to remain elegant even as trends change.

options.label: Personal
options.desc: I want it to evolve with my life and continue telling my story.

options.label: Impressive
options.desc: I want it to have a strong identity and leave an impression.

options.label: Comfortable
options.desc: I want it to feel familiar, relaxed and welcoming for years to come.

options.label: Connected
options.desc: I want it to age naturally and develop a stronger relationship with its surroundings over time.

questions.endNote: Architectural insight: A successful home is not designed only for the day it is completed. Materials, proportions, flexibility and the relationship with surroundings influence how a space ages.

Contemporary Luxury.subtitle: Bold Geometry · Statement Materials · Layered Grandeur
Contemporary Luxury.description: Defined by strong geometric forms, statement materials like rich marble, warm timber, and polished brass accents. Features carefully controlled, dramatic lighting and a grand sense of volume crafted to leave an unforgettable impression.
Contemporary Luxury.spatialVibe: Sculpted opulence, high-impact focal drama & tailored refinement.

Japandi.subtitle: Warm Minimalist · Tactile Serenity · Organic Comfort
Japandi.description: A harmonious synthesis of Scandinavian warmth and Japanese functional minimalism. Emphasizes warm wood tones, tactile textured surfaces, soft natural lighting, and comfortable, welcoming spaces designed for mindful, clutter-free everyday living.
Japandi.spatialVibe: Calm visual quiet, organic warmth & understated balance.

Tropical Modern.subtitle: Biophilic Harmony · Verdant Courtyards · Breathing Spaces
Tropical Modern.description: Blurs the threshold between indoor sanctuary and outdoor nature. Utilizes tranquil courtyards, shaded verandas, deep overhangs, and expansive glass portals that capture breezes, filtered daylight, and lush greenery that ages gracefully with time.
Tropical Modern.spatialVibe: Deeply relaxing, indoor-outdoor flow & climate-responsive serenity.

Modern Minimal.subtitle: Clean Lines · Uncluttered Restraint · Pure Light
Modern Minimal.description: Rooted in simplicity, visual quiet, and spatial discipline. Features crisp geometric planes, concealed integrated storage, seamless circulation, and a restrained monochromatic palette that elevates soft natural daylight into the primary design element.
Modern Minimal.spatialVibe: Impeccable order, visual quiet & calming spatial clarity.

Contemporary Indian.subtitle: Rooted Heritage · Artisanal Warmth · Evolving Story
Contemporary Indian.description: A sensitive dialogue between cultural roots and contemporary aesthetics. Combines balanced proportions, native stone, terracotta, timber, cane, and terrazzo to craft a home that feels familiar, durable, and built to celebrate life stories across generations.
Contemporary Indian.spatialVibe: Grounded permanence, cultural depth & evolving warmth.

Classical Indian.subtitle: Artisanal Craftsmanship · Heritage Proportions · Regal Depth
Classical Indian.description: Rooted in timeless cultural heritage and artisanal mastery. Celebrates traditional balanced proportions, earthy lime plaster walls, terracotta accents, intricately carved timber, and vibrant patterned fabrics that bestow a stately, sanctuary-like presence.
Classical Indian.spatialVibe: Artisanal authenticity, regal gravitas & crafted timelessness.

Modern Style.subtitle: Dynamic Living · Flexible Volumes · Strong Focal Points
Modern Style.description: Designed for expressive, dynamic contemporary lifestyles and hosting. Features versatile open-plan rooms, strong focal features, adaptable lighting systems, and crisp materials that comfortably adjust between intimate downtime and lively gatherings.
Modern Style.spatialVibe: Flexible openness, vibrant hosting & dynamic modern comfort.

Neo Classical.subtitle: Symmetrical Harmony · Stately Grandeur · Timeless Elegance
Neo Classical.description: Inspired by classical symmetry, noble proportions, and architectural hierarchy. Showcases distinct formal spaces, layered cornices and mouldings, statement chandeliers, and curated luxury materials that remain elegant even as passing trends change.
Neo Classical.spatialVibe: Generational prestige, formal grandeur & dignified elegance.

Industrial.subtitle: Structural Honesty · Open Loft Volumes · Raw Authenticity
Industrial.description: Celebrates unadorned structural honesty and unconventional volume. Highlights exposed concrete walls, blackened structural steel, expansive Crittall-style glass panels, and open circulation that together create an authentic, edgy, and spacious architectural statement.
Industrial.spatialVibe: High-volume openness, raw tactile edge & structural authenticity.
